item.title: Prenatal Lead Exposure Affects the Aging Brain
item.description: A biological time capsule reveals a 60-year secret. Scientists find that lead exposure in the womb can act as a "cognitive accelerator," adding years to the aging brain.

item.title: Tumors Command the Brain to Suppress T Cells
item.description: Tumors aren't just rogue cells; they are master manipulators. Scientists find cancer "calls" the brain to request an immune-suppressing shield.

item.title: Brain Organoids Learn to Solve Tasks
item.description: Researchers demonstrate goal-directed learning in brain organoids, training lab-grown tissue to solve the "cart-pole" balance task via electrical feedback.

item.title: The Brain Ignores Itching When You’re Stressed
item.description: In a crisis, the last thing you want to do is scratch. Scientists discover the brain's "mute button" that silences itch during stress—and why it fails in chronic conditions.

item.title: Moving Beyond Dopamine to Treat Schizophrenia
item.description: Dopamine isn't the whole story. A massive new review outlines the next generation of schizophrenia therapies that target the immune system, the gut, and cognitive receptors.

item.title: Expertise Protects Against Cognitive Decline
item.description: It’s not just a hobby; it’s a brain workout. Scientists find that the intense perception and memory required for birdwatching literally reorganizes the brain for better aging.

item.title: Chatbots Can Worsen Delusions and Mania
item.description: A digital helping hand or a dangerous mirror? New research reveals how AI chatbots can consolidate delusions and worsen symptoms for those with severe mental illness.

item.title: Brain May Treat Seizures As Memories
item.description: The brain is a master at learning, but sometimes it learns the wrong things. Scientists find that sleep after a seizure acts as a "save button" for epilepsy.

item.title: Neurons Use RNA “Tentacles” to Survive Starvation
item.description: Researchers discover that neurons pair inactive ribosomes using RNA "tentacles" to save energy and survive during periods of starvation or stress.

item.title: MRI Risk: Nerve Implants Can Trigger Unintended Shocks
item.description: A hidden danger in the magnet. Scientists discover that vagus nerve implants can be "tricked" into firing by MRI fields, causing unintended pain for patients.
